sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE followed by clipping at \(c/2\) and mass renormalization. The half-open-cell lift selector returns \(\widehat a_p,\widehat\phi_p,\widehat a_T,\widehat\phi_T\) and uses a fixed measurable fallback off its regular domain. Covariance pilots are two-fold cross-fitted, include the harmonic translation score, and are evaluated by adjoint elliptic solves; \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) is added before every block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: The intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes identification and exact four-input derivative are established, including nonzero harmonic translation modes. This round proves the fixed-center Green-aligned product-Hellinger alternatives, their \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)/n\) separation, and the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) size of both selected-translation changes; it also verifies the uniform-law Fourier reduction and a smooth nonzero separable witness. The general-density critical Gaussian limit, full four-cell covariance convergence, adjoint consistency, simultaneous asymptotic coverage, and uniform upper risk remain conditional on one explicit analytic gap: transformed-KDE stability at an estimated moving pole plus the uniform nonlinear tame remainder.

project_justification.gap: Published transport central-limit results do not prove a pointwise gradient limit in dimension two for general variable coefficients with a generated target, and published global minimax bounds do not supply the nested four-cell pointwise logarithmic local experiment. The remaining gap is specifically uniform shrinking-bandwidth control of transformed kernels, estimated coefficients and poles, and the nested nonlinear remainder.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, a Green gradient has logarithmically divergent variance, while nesting makes each control sample enter both directly and through the generated target. Independent samples prevent cancellation. The fixed-center converse can be proved without resolving the harder uniform random-pole expansion.
project_justification.fill: The note establishes intrinsic torus identification, a translation-aware lift, the exact nested derivative, bandwidth feasibility, fixed-center annular Green alternatives with explicit harmonic-translation control, a uniform-law Fourier benchmark, and a smooth nonzero separable benchmark. It records the candidate four-cell covariance and adjoint ellipse procedure, but labels their general-density asymptotic validity as open until the transformed-KDE moving-pole and nonlinear tame estimates are proved.

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates cyclic-comonotone changes-in-changes and the Card--Krueger application but does not prove the intrinsic torus identification used here. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies periodized-KDE and Monge--Ampere tools and proves the uniform-law dimension-two special case, while leaving general variable coefficients open. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supports one smooth density-path linearization; the exact four-input generated-target derivative is established in this note. The 2026 Green-influence results identify pole singularities but do not supply the shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical limit, and GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT excludes pointwise gradients. HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin concern global one-map risk; the present fixed-center annular construction supplies a distinct pointwise logarithmic lower-bound mechanism. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand motivates simultaneous transport uncertainty in one dimension, but the proposed bivariate ellipses still await singular-adjoint consistency.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved analytic module is uniform control of the variable-coefficient pole after transformed KDE smoothing. The required numerical kill test remains: on one nonseparable smooth torus law with nonconstant \(f_{T0}/f_{C0}\), compute cellwise adjoint covariance increments at \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\), refine the PDE mesh until discretization changes are negligible, and separately track generated-target, harmonic, coefficient, and pole remainders. A slope discrepancy, a logarithmically divergent normalized remainder, or failure of \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) pole accuracy invalidates the proposed general-density inference spine. The fixed-center local lower bound does not resolve this random-pole problem.
body.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of intrinsic torus causal identification, the exact nested derivative, bandwidth arithmetic, a fixed-center Hellinger-local logarithmic lower-bound construction whose constants \(c_0(P_0)\), \(\kappa(P_0)\), and sample threshold may depend on the center's interior margins, the uniform-law covariance reduction, and a nonzero smooth separable witness. No general-density critical CLT, adjoint covariance consistency, simultaneous asymptotic coverage, or class-uniform upper-risk theorem is claimed until oeq:uniform-critical-control is resolved. The ellipses are fixed-grid procedures, not confidence bands over the torus.
